disagreement.point: X 'When a prostitute murders her paramour, she shall be burnt alive' vs Y 'If a man causes her distress ... forces her into water'; source: पुरुषं [घ्नत्याश्]चिताप्रतापोऽप्सु प्रवेशनं वा (penalty falls on the woman; OCR garbled here)

choice_note: X keeps Sanskrit terms in parentheses beside an English gloss (bhoga, áyati, kusílava, rúpájivá) and expands clauses for sense; Y translates terms into plain English ('those who live by beauty') and stays clause-for-clause, also 'courtesan' vs 'prostitute' for gaṇikā.

disagreement.point: X 'A hundred yojanas wide and thirty yojanas long' vs Y 'ten yoyanas in width and twenty in length'; source: शतयोजनविस्तीर्णा त्रिंशद्योजनआयता (Y likely follows another recension; conversely Y is nearer on घनैरिवातपापाये)

choice_note: X gives plain modern numbered verse-by-verse lines with glossed names and 'demons'; Y gives continuous elevated Victorian epic prose keeping 'Rakshasas', 'chamaras' — accessible crib vs period-voice reading.

disagreement.point: X 'the first, third, and fifth syllables don't matter' vs Y 'the first, third and fifth lines are of no consequence'; source: 一三五不論，二四六分明 (positions within a line, not lines)

choice_note: X modernises: pinyin, identifies poets (Wang Wei, Du Fu, Li Bai) with the original style-names in notes, translates lodge names; Y keeps Wade-Giles style-names as written (Wang Mo-chieh, Lao T'u) and a wordy Victorian narrative voice, and sets the Lu You couplet as verse.

disagreement.point: X 'The mark of continuity: Relying on wisdom, it generates consciousness of suffering' vs Y 'Emotion. This follows consciousness and produces joy and sorrow'; source: 二者相續相依於智故生其苦樂覺心 (and 執取相: X 'mark of grasping' vs Y 'Attention')

choice_note: Y is a loose paraphrase that replaces the scholastic terms (相續相, 執取相, 智) with unrelated everyday words and adds 'false ideas ... partial enlightenment' unflagged; the contrast is not two legitimate renderings of the same terms.

disagreement.point: X 'A large stone is not raised with such facility by animal strength' vs Y 'War is not as easily provoked by living beings as it is terrible'; source: न तथोत्थाप्यते ग्रावा प्राणिभिर्दारुणा यथा (OCR: यावा ... दारुणं)

choice_note: X renders the upāyas in English ('gentle means, gifts, sowing divisions') and sets each maxim as a numbered gnomic verse; Y keeps sama/dana/bheda with glosses and runs the verses as quoted prose, also translating the Bengali paraphrase.

disagreement.point: X 'To those who are not good, I am also good. Virtue is good' vs Y 'and thus (all) get to be good'; source: 不善者吾亦善之德善矣 (德 as 'virtue' vs read as 得)

choice_note: X leaves the terse lines bare and open ('no fixed heart', 'Virtue is good', 'muddies his heart'); Y resolves them into an interpretation but marks every supplied word in parentheses ('(to me)', '(all)') — open literal vs flagged interpretive.

disagreement.point: X 'I offer with the eye of the sacrifice, the beginning, the face' vs Y 'Of the sacrifice the eye, beginning, and face; with voice'; source: यज्ञस्य चक्षुः प्रभृतिर्मुखं च वाचा श्रोत्रेण मनसा जुहोमि (चक्षुः is not instrumental)

choice_note: Verse 6 close: X follows the printed reading and the commentary, 'great in splendor, rejoice' (त्विषा मादयन्ताम्); Y follows an emended reading, 'revel on the oblation'. X also translates the commentary's 'mental sacrifice' gloss; Y is a bare crib with Sanskrit words in parentheses.

disagreement.point: X 'by these nine tests the inferior man is discovered' vs Y 'even a man of little worth will acquire them'; source: 九徵至不肖人得矣 (also 如而夫者…呂鉅: X 'ordinary men … haughty stride' vs Y 'like Lü Ju')
